evidence:
DIMENSION WEIGHTS. task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean): '[gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0', '[weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2', '[floors] functional = 0.05'. This is exactly the delivery profile in SKILL.md:28 ('functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 ... behind two zero-weight gates and a functional floor') and the internal workbook note E45 ('Functionality has 60 pecent'). task/tests/tools/score.py is also identical to the template; score.py:46 computes sum(w*score)/sum(w) and :48 zeroes the reward unless gates and floors pass. No 'weight' key sits in any [judge] block; weights appear only on [[criterion]] entries. Gate criteria (1 render, 2 constraints) are binary at weight 1.0 under aggregation = "all_pass", so gates carry no reward mass.

PER-CRITERION WEIGHTS (parsed with tomllib). Functional: 43 binary criteria, weights 1.0 (17 criteria), 1.5 (20) and 2.0 (6), total 59.0, aggregation weighted_mean. The 2.0 criteria are cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (judge.toml:99), cw_same_line_carets (:117), cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo (:189), cw_last_good_recovery (:288), cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (:306) and cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (:396). These are the deepest multi-step behaviours and map onto the headline asks of instruction.md ('paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source ... without losing a draft when another tab saves first'). The 1.0 criteria are single-surface basics (typing/join, caret navigation, mouse selection, find, replace current, basic run, HTML preview, console order, etc.). The spread is only 2:1, so no criterion dominates: the heaviest functional criterion is 2/59 = 3.39% of the dimension = 2.03% of reward, the lightest 1.02%. By area: editor 21 criteria / 28.0 points (47.5%), runtime and preview boundary 14 / 19.5 (33.1%), persistence and multi-tab 8 / 11.5 (19.5%), consistent with overview.md 'The editor should be a useful tool in its own right'. Every functional criterion grades observable behaviour through real input; none grades DOM structure, file layout or style, so no structure/style item is weighted above real functionality inside the dimension. Polish: 6 binary criteria all at 1.0 (keyboard reachability, feedback, focus return, undo/redo availability, unsaved marker, 390 px usability) - each is behaviour required by ui.md, equal weights are defensible. Visual: 3 likert criteria, points = 5, all at 1.0, each with anchors 5..0.

MAXIMUM NON-FUNCTIONAL CONTRIBUTION (skill sanity check). Polish + visual are capped at 0.40 by the frozen template. They cannot be collected by a shell: both gates must pass first (a custom non-textarea editor that takes typing, and a Save read back from an independent context), and functional must exceed 0.05, i.e. more than 2.95 of 59 weight points. One 2.0 criterion alone (0.0339) or two 1.0 criteria (0.0339) do not clear the floor; at least 3.0 points are needed. Weak-app check: an app that passes the gates, passes three 1.0 functional basics and is perfectly polished and styled scores 0.6*3/59 + 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.4305. A fully functional but plain app with polish 3/6 and visual likert 3 scores 0.6 + 0.1 + 0.2*(0.5 or 0.6) = 0.80-0.82. Function still dominates the ordering, and the 0.40 ceiling is template policy that this row must not alter (assignment: 'Do not ... alter shared harness/scoring policy').

RUN EVIDENCE. No configured judge run exists for these bytes. The only surviving hosted artefact for the earlier candidate that I could read, verifier/scored/rewardkit.log, says 'functional: 1.0 / polish: 1.0 / visual: 0.9167', which is arithmetically consistent with 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.2*0.9167 = 0.9833 as quoted in the index, i.e. the dimension weights are applied as written. That is an earlier candidate, not a measurement of these bytes.

EVIDENCE INDEX HASHES - NOT VERIFIABLE. All 22 artefacts listed in raw-evidence-index.json are absent at the stated paths at review time (22 of 22 missing, so no hash could be checked). qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict contains only results/build.log and results/restart.log (directory mtime 2 Oct 20:27); run_golden.sh, tests/*.cjs, results/*.json and the three PNGs are not there. Under run-outputs/.../run-4e686738.../colderwater-playground-devtools__Rc3y2sT only trial.log, verifier/app.log, verifier/app-restart.log and the two rewardkit.log files exist; result.json, verifier/reward.json and both reward-details.json are missing, and the run-6e537d14 directory is missing entirely. This row's verdict does not depend on those artefacts (weights are static source facts), but the owner should restore them or correct the index before any reviewer relies on it.

NOTES (not defects for this row).
(1) Per-criterion reward mass is inverted across dimensions because of the criterion counts under the fixed 0.6/0.2/0.2 split: each visual likert criterion is worth 0.2/3 = 6.67% of reward and each polish criterion 0.2/6 = 3.33%, while the heaviest functional criterion is worth 2.03% and cw_save_reload_restart (weight 1.5) 1.53%. For example 'colour harmony, consistency of buttons and fields' (cw_visual_component_finish) carries about 4.4 times the reward of saved work surviving a process restart. In aggregate functionality still outweighs style 0.6 to 0.4, the split is frozen, and reducing functional criteria to fix the ratio would cost coverage, so I record this rather than fail it.
(2) cw_js_semantic_coloring is weighted 1.5 (functional/judge.toml:171), above cw_basic_run_output (:216), cw_html_preview (:225), cw_error_message_and_line (:234), cw_history_restore_retry (:369) and cw_restore_request_repeat_safe (:378), all 1.0. Token colouring is the most presentation-like item in the functional dimension; its criterion does grade real token classification (five categories, function name identical at declaration and call) and Run is implicitly exercised by roughly twenty other criteria, so the effective weight of core Run is far higher than 1.0. Equalising colouring to 1.0, or raising cw_history_restore_retry (a three-part conjunctive flow covering inspect, restore and a concurrent old-revision restore) to 1.5, would make the scale more self-consistent.
(3) The 1.0/1.5/2.0 tiers are not documented anywhere in the task; the rationale above is my reading of difficulty and brief emphasis, not an authored statement.
(4) Likert normalisation is done inside RewardKit, which is not in the frozen tree; the 0.80-0.82 example above brackets both plausible mappings and nothing in this row depends on which one applies.
